title: Temporary Construction Permits 2026: Conditions and Documents
desc: Can you build on land that is zoned but not yet reclaimed? Conditions, documents and timelines for temporary construction permits under Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
summary: Where land is covered by a zoning plan but the State has not yet reclaimed it, owners can apply for a temporary construction permit; this article summarises the conditions, documents and self-demolition undertaking under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 217/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Many land plots fall within planning for roads, parks and similar projects but have gone unreclaimed for years. The owner can still build or repair a house if granted a temporary construction permit – one of the three types of permit under Clause 1, Article 43 of the Construction Law 2025.
h2
1. What is a temporary construction permit?
p

Under Clause 2, Article 44 of the Construction Law 2025, this permit is issued for works in an area with a zoning plan that has been approved and announced but not yet implemented and for which no land reclamation decision has been issued. The work may stand only until the expiry date stated in the permit. It is also the only type of permit that does not have to conform to the zoning plan (Point b, Clause 1, Article 44).
h2
2. Conditions for issuance
p
Under Article 52 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP, the work must satisfy all of the following:
ul
It is located in an area with an approved and announced zoning plan that has not yet been implemented and for which no land reclamation decision has been issued.
It conforms to the scale, height and duration of existence set by the provincial People's Committee for each area (or approved for the specific work).
It conforms to the land use purpose stated on the lawful land documents under Article 55.
It ensures structural safety for the work itself and neighbouring works, fire prevention and fighting, and environmental protection; the design is prepared as required (Clauses 3 and 4, Article 50).

The project owner undertakes to demolish the work themselves when the permitted period ends and a land reclamation decision is issued; if they do not, the work will be forcibly demolished and they bear all demolition costs.
h2
3. When only repair or renovation is allowed
p
If the area is already covered by a commune-level land use plan, a temporary permit is not issued for new construction, only for repair and renovation (Clause 4, Article 52).
p

Exception: if 2 consecutive years have passed since the commune-level land use plan was approved and the State has still not issued a land reclamation decision or allowed a change of land use purpose, and the plan has not been adjusted or cancelled (or has been but not announced), the land user may apply for a temporary permit.
h2
4. Documents, place of submission and processing time
ul

The application documents are the same as for a construction permit for the relevant type of work or detached house; only the title of the application form changes to "Application for a temporary construction permit" (Article 62).

For a detached house of a household or individual, the dossier consists of the application, lawful land documents, a set of design drawings and a written undertaking to ensure the safety of adjoining works (Article 60).
Submit online through the National Public Service Portal; the commune-level People's Committee issues permits for detached houses (Clause 1, Article 53).
Detached houses: the permit is issued within 7 working days of receipt of a complete and valid dossier (Point b, Clause 1, Article 54).
p
For the general procedure, see Procedure for a Detached House Construction Permit 2026.
h2
5. What happens when the permitted period expires?
ul

If the permitted period ends and the zoning plan has still not been implemented: the permitting authority issues a notice extending the period of existence; the owner may keep using the house until a land reclamation decision is issued. To build anew or carry out further repairs, a new temporary permit must be applied for (Clauses 1 and 3, Article 52).
If the State reclaims the land before the period stated in the permit ends: compensation and site clearance are carried out under land law (Clause 4, Article 52).

Building not in accordance with the temporary permit: a detached house is fined VND 15–20 million (the rate for organisations; individuals pay half) and the violating part may have to be demolished (Clauses 4 and 14, Article 25 of Decree 339/2026/ND-CP; Clause 4, Article 5).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The scale, height and permitted duration of works are set separately by the provincial People's Committee (not yet in our library); ask the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located before designing.
